title: Autoscaler: add predictive scaling signal provider interface + staleness checks
author: Mei Lin
description: Summary: This PR introduces a pluggable forecast provider interface for Dedicated autoscaling and wires it into the autoscaler signal pipeline with strict staleness validation and safe fallback to reactive scaling when forecasts are unavailable/invalid. This is intentionally scoped to plumbing + safety; it does not change the default scaling policy behavior unless predictive mode is explicitly enabled via feature flag and config. Motivation: Enterprise Dedicated customers have predictable traffic ramps (time-of-day, scheduled jobs) and want scaling to happen ahead of demand. Before we can blend predictive and reactive signals, we need a stable interface boundary, observability for availability/staleness, and deterministic fallback behavior. Design overview: - New interface `ForecastProvider` (control-plane friendly but implemented in fleet autoscaler for now) that returns a time series forecast for a deployment/region for a configured horizon. - Staleness checks: forecasts are rejected if `generated_at` is older than `max_forecast_age` (default 10m) or if the newest forecast point is older than `max_point_age` (default 5m). - Fallback behavior: if the provider errors, times out, returns empty, or fails validation, we mark prediction as unavailable and continue using reactive signals only. We also emit a structured reason code for auditability and metrics. - Feature gating: predictive reads are behind `dedicated_predictive_autoscaling` (account/deployment-scoped flag handled in later PR); this PR includes only a local kill-switch in autoscaler config and a safety default to disabled. - Determinism: the autoscaler loop records both `requested_prediction` and `prediction_status` (available/unavailable + reason) in the decision context so downstream PRs can clamp/bound/choose signals without ambiguity. API / types: - `ForecastRequest { deployment_id, region, model_id?, horizon_seconds, step_seconds, now }` - `ForecastResponse { generated_at, points: [{ ts, rps, tokens_per_sec? }], confidence?: 0..1, source }` - Reason codes for invalidation: `provider_timeout`, `provider_error`, `stale_generated_at`, `stale_points`, `empty_forecast`, `invalid_shape`. Observability included: - `dedicated_autoscaler_prediction_available{deployment_id,region}` (0/1) (NOTE: deployment_id label will be replaced with hashed id in metrics PR; left as TODO but gated behind debug metric sink in prod). - `dedicated_autoscaler_prediction_rejected_total{reason,region}` counter. - Decision log field `prediction.status` and `prediction.reason` added to the autoscaler structured log event (not the compliance audit log; that’s in ENG-22146). Testing: - Unit tests for staleness validation, shape validation, and timeout fallback. - Integration test with a fake provider simulating partial outages and slow responses; ensures autoscaler loop continues and does not block scaling decisions. Rollout / safety: - No behavior change by default. Predictive mode remains disabled. - On provider failure, we always fall back to reactive. No scale-to-zero risk from missing predictions (explicitly handled: null/empty forecast is treated as unavailable, not as zero demand). Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Policy-level blending and arbitration between reactive saturation/queue depth and prediction (ENG-22140/ENG-22142). - Metrics naming/cardinality alignment to observability standards (ENG-22143). - Account/deployment scoped feature flag plumbing (ENG-22148).
commits: autoscaler/predictive: introduce ForecastProvider interface + request/response types
autoscaler/predictive: implement staleness + shape validation (generated_at + point freshness)
autoscaler/predictive: add timeout wrapper + fallback to reactive on errors
autoscaler/logging: include prediction status + rejection reason in decision context logs
tests: unit tests for validation + integration test with fake provider
review_conversation: Vanessa Ortiz (review): Can we guarantee the autoscaler loop never blocks on the provider call? If forecast service is slow, I don’t want it to extend decision latency or cause missed ticks.

Mei Lin (author): Yes — provider call is wrapped with a 250ms timeout (configurable). On timeout we mark prediction unavailable with reason `provider_timeout` and proceed. Added an integration test asserting the loop tick completes under slow provider.

Sana Farid (review): Staleness semantics: generated_at vs point timestamps. We’ve seen cases where generated_at is fresh but the forecast points lag due to backfill. Please validate both, and add explicit reason codes so we can measure which failure mode we hit.
Mei Lin (author): Updated validation to check both `generatedAt` and `lastPoint.ts`. Added reason codes `stale_generated_at` and `stale_points`, plus a counter `prediction_rejected_total{reason}`.
Jordan Lee (review): Minor: please avoid using deployment_id as a metric label in prod. This will explode cardinality. Can you gate it or leave TODO wired for later?

Mei Lin (author): Good call. I gated the per-deployment gauge behind the existing debug metrics sink (only enabled in staging/canary). In prod we emit only region-level counters until ENG-22143 lands with hashed IDs / approved label set.
Rafael Mendes (review): Please confirm the fallback cannot be interpreted as zero demand. We had prior incidents where null got cast to 0 and scaled down aggressively.
Mei Lin (author): Confirmed. `null` / empty forecasts are treated as unavailable; we never convert them into a numeric target. Added a regression unit test `empty_forecast_does_not_change_desired`.
Vanessa Ortiz (approval): Looks good. The timeout + reason codes are the right safety baseline. Approved once CI is green.
Samantha Roy (approval): Approved. Telemetry fields are consistent with our structured logging conventions.
release_notes: Internal: Dedicated autoscaler now supports a forecast provider interface with staleness validation and safe fallback to reactive scaling when predictions are unavailable.
